questions.question: Explain equilibrium in the four-sector circular flow using the leakages-injections equality, then calculate and interpret the effect of a R10 billion investment injection when the marginal propensity to consume is 0,6.
questions.expected_answer: The four participants — households, businesses, the state and the foreign sector — are linked by real flows of factors and goods and money flows of income and spending. The economy is in equilibrium when leakages equal injections: S + T + M = I + G + X, equivalently when Y = C + I + G + (X − M). Savings, taxes and imports drain spending from the flow; investment, government spending and exports feed it. The multiplier is 1 ÷ (1 − mpc) = 1 ÷ (1 − 0,6) = 1 ÷ 0,4 = 2,5, so the R10 billion injection ultimately raises income by 2,5 × R10 billion = R25 billion. The mechanism is successive spending rounds: recipients of the initial R10 billion spend 60 cents of each rand, those recipients spend 60 cents of each rand again, and the rounds shrink as saving, tax and import leakages drain each cycle. The multiplier is larger the higher the mpc, because more of each round is passed on before it leaks away.

questions.question: A data-response question shows the rand weakening against the dollar. Describe, in words, the demand-and-supply graph of the foreign exchange market that explains the movement, and evaluate the consequences for South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: The graph places the rand price of one dollar on the vertical axis and the quantity of dollars on the horizontal. The demand curve for dollars — from importers, South Africans travelling abroad and capital outflows — slopes downward; the supply curve — from exporters, inbound tourists and foreign investment — slopes upward; their intersection sets the exchange rate. The rand weakens when demand for dollars shifts right (more imports, capital flight) or supply shifts left (weaker exports, investor withdrawal): the equilibrium rand price of the dollar rises, which is depreciation under South Africa's free-floating system. Evaluation must run both ways: exporters gain because South African goods become cheaper abroad, tourism gains because foreign money stretches further, and import-competing firms get relief; but imported oil, machinery and medicine cost more, raising transport costs and fuelling cost-push inflation, and the poor are hit through food and taxi fares. A strong conclusion notes the net effect depends on import-dependence and whether exporters exploit the price advantage, and that the Reserve Bank may smooth extreme swings but does not fix the rate.

questions.question: Distinguish between economic growth and economic development, outline the demand-side and supply-side approaches to promoting them, and assess South Africa's policy record from the RDP to the NDP.
questions.expected_answer: Growth is the sustained increase in real GDP; development is the broader improvement in living standards, capabilities and choices — growth can occur without development if rising output leaves poverty and inequality untouched. The demand-side approach stimulates spending through expansionary monetary policy (lower interest rates, open market transactions) and fiscal policy (progressive income tax, grants and other redistribution); the supply-side approach raises productive capacity by improving market efficiency, business efficiency and reducing the cost of doing business, including infrastructure and skills. South Africa's sequence: the RDP (1994) rebuilt basic services — housing, water, electricity; GEAR (1996) pursued macroeconomic stability and fiscal discipline; AsgiSA and JIPSA targeted growth bottlenecks and priority skills; the EPWP created temporary public employment; the New Growth Path (2010) prioritised job creation; the NDP sets 2030 targets for eliminating poverty and reducing inequality, supported by industrial instruments such as IDZs and later SEZs. A fair assessment credits stabilisation and service extension but notes persistent unemployment, inequality and implementation failure, concluding that design has outrun delivery — an own-judgement line that earns the higher-order marks.
